reviews.text: Good game for the price range it is in. Spend hours to kill as many bad guys as possible. Make a build using armor, weapons, and abilities with roguelike choices. Solo it is comparable to other games in this type of genre. What is nice about this version compared to a lot of other games is the co-op. You can make some really great supporting builds to push the party forward.

There are many Survivor games. Some are great, some are good, some are average, some are bad and some are Stolen Realm Survivors. The only pro of this game is that the content is very limited. So you don't suffer for a very long time.

I put about 21 hours into the demo and unlocked nearly everything except for two weapons. When the full game launched for $9, I was surprised to find that the demo was the entire game. There were no meaningful additions, despite the store page showcasing what appeared to be extra abilities, content, and maps that made it seem like the full release would offer more. That made the launch feel extremely disappointing and honestly misleading. I understand demos are sometimes meant to represent the core experience, but charging for what was effectively the exact same content left me feeling deceived and regretting the purchase.

There is a great shell and excellent potential here. Obviously it's not perfect but what we do have is a lot to work with if we're looking for hours of entertainment. Big plus to be able to play co-op, which is where most survivor games are lacking. Seamless transition between keyboard/mouse and gamepad is another plus. Both methods feel fine to use but a few small complaints with gamepad like navigating the map and not being able to mouse-over certain things like quest rewards to see a description. UI needs a bit of work, high contrast was definitely a step in the right direction. Basically, knowing it's a bit flawed will not stop me from enjoying the hell out of this game with friends. Hopefully, it will be actively improved over time too. Recommended.

After topping the leaderboard on the demo for a while, I was excited to finally get the new content CLEARLY displayed on the steam page. New environments, skills, items, etc. Turns out the full release that you pay for is exactly the same content as the free demo. If you're going to release a game when you have a free demo, you should have new content. Also...showing content in your steam assets that aren't in game? That's deceptive as hell. I wanted to leave a positive review, but this was an insulting release at best. You can't afford to make mistakes like this as an indie dev. It's already hard enough to find players. Don't deceive the ones you have.
I played throughout closed and beta testing, and this dev team has put a lot of work into this. $10 for a very good roguelike with multiplayer and leaderboards is a huge W for the genre.

Spent some time in the playtest (around 140 hrs), then got notified that the game was released, bought it mostly to support the devs since it's not that pricey in my region. I think we should support small devs since major publishers mostly pump out trash these days and treat players like garbage. I'd say that within that gap between the moment I stopped playing the playtest and the release the game did improve in some ways. In some ways it didn't. And I'm talking only about the solo experience. The UI is much more pleasant, but still clunky, especially the path selection system, which would work so much better if it was just 2-3 portals opening in-game after a stage is finished, not an additional menu. A lot of builds I used to squeeze into leaderboards are now either nerfed heavily or complete trash for some reason. Also, it feels like almost every important stat was nerfed, while some weaker stats like Armor never took off. The quest system is ok, not sure if it is fitting for this type of game, but it does something, although gameplay limitations don't really allow quests to become something special. During the playtest, if you knew a couple of game-breaking builds and managed to roll those, you could pretty much oblitarate anything. I think this was what they were trying to remove with all those nerfs and item changes, so one wouldn't get into a typical situation with these games: you either get all you need by a certain point and dominate, or just end the descent early when you get a botched run. Did they manage that? Sort of. I tried my go-to build, rolled it perfectly, but since the legendary set I used it with is now completely useless, and shrines are no longer available on all stages, I did fall behind and failed miserably early on, around stages 25-30. An I know that there are still broken builds, the leaderboards won't like, they're just built around different stats and items now. To sum up, I'd say that sadly, I had more fun with this game during the playtest than now, but it's just me. On release I expected to see more interesting stats, combinations, interactions between different weapons, skills and procs, but what I got were limitations, nerfs and additional menus. I did spot a couple of new enemies, stages and bosses, which is neat. I cannot recommend this game, but I still left a thumbs up to cheer the devs so they don't give up. P. S. Steam page trailer for this game is so different from the actual gameplay I wonder if this is even legal.

No lifed this game with a buddy for over 12 hours and I think its pretty decent. Since I own the stolen realm og game it was about $8 and id say I got my moneys worth for sure. I did not play the demo at all so I can see how it can be a bit of a botched release for them after reading some of the reviews, idk if you got 5+ hours out of a free demo then the game cant be that bad. There's 3 acts to the game and once you beat the third act the game enters a infinite play mode where it shuffles up the stages and bosses into continuous runs until you die, and you dont really get a choice to not play infinite if you want all 3 acts. The only way to really get far in the infinite mode past act three is to have a op/broken build. Then its mostly boring even with a broken build because you for the most part one shot everything and it becomes a war of attrition to see how little you value your time, and since most stages are set to a timer of 1 minute you have to sit through one shotting everything. The bosses however dont scale that well in the infinite mode and they end up being the quickest part of the run since you one shot them as well, but when you kill a boss the stage ends so you dont have to sit there a minute. The leaderboards are tracked by how many stages you complete, and at the time of this review the highest score was 135 stages, so with around a minute a room that run took a bit over 2 hours. The only other motivation to play into the infinite section with a broken build is to try and get/buy gear or get more meta currency that you also use to buy gear. The gear in the meta store is randomized so if you want certain pieces you have to start a run and die to reset what's in the shop. I think overall the infinite mode needs more work, and maybe add a mode that is just the 3 acts without the infinite part but with a few extra stages to allow builds to fill out and you get some bonus currency at the end when you complete it. Especially since upgrades from leveling eventually run out in infinite. Decent build variety, some are stronger than others, and you can see whatever someone's build is on the leaderboard to check what the op ones are. You get to the 3rd act pretty quickly when youve played for a bit so for me the fun has been trying out different combos, then going a little into the infinite stages to see how it does. More fun with a friend for sure, it felt a bit slower when I ran a couple solo. There's some synergy builds you can do with a buddy or both just do your own thing. Overall if you got a buddy and like survivors its not bad to kill time, and ill keep up with the game whenever there are updates or feel like playing some coop survivors.

The current character roster is diverse, the build options are varied, and in general watching enemies get flung around the map as you bash them is very fun. The game truly shines when playing with friends, coordinating builds, figuring out what helps support each other, and chatting as you get into the higher depths. Looking forward to seeing what Burst2Flame does going forward!

TL:DR - I'm positive-neutral for a $10 purchase. Would love to give a neutral rating. I'm 40 hours in release, and at least that much in the preceding demo builds. Worth the price for the playtime. The release version itself was a small jump from the pre-release demo with small with additional events, a few weapons (via events) and some new item choices. There are valid complaints that some content advertised is absent and still visible in the trailer video (that long bridge fight? The chest? Never seen either in game). There seems to be more meaningful content in development, and it would have been nice to have gotten something notable at release. The meta has become a few key skill & item selections dominating the daily leaderboard. That imbalance is obvious in groups if friends optimize differently. There is also a feeling that after 80, the game is entirely bullet hell avoidance where dodge, block, armor & health choices are almost meaningless. The one-shot is how the runs ends. On the other hand, if you're that high, you've effectively 'beat' the game's mechanics and it's patience & reflexes to continue higher.

Burst2Flame Games has made really good and positive changes since launch. If the review was from launch time just ignore it. They gave people the full game as a beta access and this is a small indie developer and people got mad that the game wasn't different right away, chill people. Was there issues at launch, yes but after the most recent updates to how skills and the game works it is really fun, addictive and a HUGE variety of viable builds and absolutely worth the money. Initially there wasn't much build diversity and certain items dominated the landscape, not anymore. Trust that Burst2Flame Games will make it right as they already came out with a small free update for some new bosses, new abilities and all sorts of stuff. Their original game Stolen Realms is an absolute blast and I am sure with some more sanding and polishing this game will be fantastic, I already have a hard time putting it down already. Current Issues I have which I imagine will be fixed in the near future as they take what the community says to heart. 1. Skill visibility / performance, late game when stuff gets pretty wild sometimes it is near impossible to see things with certain abilities, but go play some other roguelikes and tell me they don't have that issue either... With that as well certain abilities do have huge performance hits when stacked with certain things. For example, using some damaging aura, running around and having thieving (gold gain) lags the hell out of my system late game (sometimes down to <10 fps even with all settings turned down) with all the mobs going in and out of the aura and I don't have the latest and greatest of AM5, but it is the best of AM4 for gaming and I feel like that should be enough to handle this game. These need to be addressed over time. 2. Random bugs here and there, nothing game breaking but just some small annoying things, check the discord for what people are posting. Some it may just be descriptions not being fully laid out and other are just small bugs. 3. Better descriptions / information. Example, Branch of the Bog weapon description "Poison Cloud: Release a toxic cloud that poisons enemies within the area." What does Poison do, how much damage does it do, how often does it tick etc... I have no idea how the weapon works, what makes it work and how to min/max or utilize it best. I had tons of fun using it and playing with it getting super late game but hard to tell how to optimize and what are good/bad decisions on both upgrades and gear to equip to make the best use of it. I want to know the DETAILS of how these things and mechanics work. Give me an in game encyclopedia or better tooltips that describe exactly what is happening. Same can be said for bleed and some other things in the game, give us the information on how things work, damage %s, time things are applied for all of it. And if there is too much information in the tool tip, give us a reference source of information. Give them time to refine and polish it, but don't hesitate to buy now. 10/10 with or without rice, play and have fun.

I'd leave a neutral review, but given how free was the demo, I'm leaving this as positive. So, SRS offers you 4 slots for active skills, each you can lvl up 25 (sometimes more) times boosting it's trigger chances, damage, size and so on and you can get unlimited passives that generally affect all skills. You do this to progress through 3.5 acts (last one is rather short) or through endless. While foundation is rather good and game is interesting while you unlock stuff, once you've seen it all - there is nothing to do. After few games you would have gained enough game knowledge to not die with any build. Literally. And lategame is long and boring w/o any challenge. And has very high strain on the eyes due to ridiculous white flashes, which happen to every single skill, leveled enough. Despite that we had nearly 25h of fun with it with a friend (mostly in demo), so give it a try. Worth the money, but don't expect it to last forever.
